title: Salmon with Blueberry Balsamic Glaze
excerpt: Learn how to make a juicy seared salmon topped with an irresistible sweet-and-sour glaze of blueberries and balsamic vinegar. An elegant, quick option perfect for a special lunch.
imageAlt: Seared salmon fillet topped with a glossy glaze of blueberries and balsamic vinegar.
steps: Season the salmon fillets on both sides with salt, pepper and half of the chopped rosemary.
In a small skillet over medium heat, heat half a teaspoon of olive oil and sauté the garlic for one minute without letting it brown too much.

Add the Fresh Pick blueberries, balsamic vinegar and honey to the skillet. Cook over low heat for 7 to 8 minutes, gently mashing some of the fruit with a fork so it releases its juice and forms a thick glaze.
In another non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, heat the rest of the olive oil and cook the salmon starting skin-side down for 4 minutes until well browned and crisp.
Flip the fillets and cook for 2 to 3 more minutes depending on the desired doneness.
Serve the salmon hot and immediately top it with the glaze of high-mountain blueberries grown in Guasca, garnishing with the rest of the fresh rosemary.
tips: To keep your Fresh Pick blueberries fresh longer, store them in the refrigerator in a container lined with paper towel and wash them only right before using them.
If you prefer a completely smooth, even sauce, you can pass the glaze through a strainer before pouring it over the salmon, keeping the leftover pulp to spread on crackers or toast.
